To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lipases that degrade triacylglycerols and acylcholestrols in rat brain have a common structural basis and are stimulated by ACTH.

Tri‐[3H]-oleoylglycerols and [14C]-oleoylcholestrol were used as substrates to investigate triacylglyceride lipase and acylcholestrol lipase activities in rat brain; these two activities showed a similar sensitivity to the presence of organic solvent, sodium taurochlate and to heat treatment; the distribution of the two activities was similar in various brain regions; ACTH stimulated both activities; these data, along wth the
the TAGL and ACL of rat brain are similar in many aspects, including reaction kinetics, substrate specificities, heat stability, and regional distributions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the ACTH‐mediated stimulation of TAGL and ACL in rat brain.
the characterization of the enzymatic hydrolysis of triacylglycerols (TAG) and of acylcholesterols (ACL), which are present in the rat brain in high concentrations (1.5 and 1.2 mM, respectively).
the elucidation of a possible physiological role for the lipolytic activity in rat brain.
